q20547.en: The sign shown requires you, at narrow passages, to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

explain.short: That is exactly the meaning: at the narrow passage, oncoming vehicles go first.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'strettoie' means narrow passages: that is where this sign is used.

sceneParams.caption: Narrow passage: oncoming vehicles go first

q20548.en: The sign shown warns that, where there are roadworks, you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

explain.short: Roadworks can close half the road and make a narrow passage; this sign then tells you to let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'in presenza di lavori' (where there are roadworks) is one possible reason for the narrow passage, so the statement is still right.

sceneParams.caption: Roadworks narrow the road: let oncoming cars pass

q20549.en: The sign shown warns that you must give way to vehicles coming towards you.

explain.short: The black arrow is the oncoming traffic: those vehicles have priority over you.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'provenienti di fronte' means coming towards you, the same as 'from the opposite direction'.

sceneParams.caption: Vehicles coming towards you go first

q20550.en: The sign shown obliges you to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

explain.short: It is a rule you must follow: oncoming vehicles pass first in the narrow passage.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'senso contrario' means the opposite direction: the black arrow.

sceneParams.caption: You must give way to oncoming vehicles

q20551.en: The sign shown requires you to give way in alternating one-way traffic.

explain.short: Its official name is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato': the two directions take turns through the passage, and you give way.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'sensi unici alternati' means the two directions use the passage one at a time.

sceneParams.caption: One direction at a time: you give way

q20552.en: The sign shown, on a two-way road, comes before a narrow passage that lets only one line of vehicles through.

explain.short: The road is two-way, but at the narrow point only one line fits, so one side must wait.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'una sola fila' (only one line) is the key: two cars cannot pass side by side there.

sceneParams.caption: Only one line fits: one side waits

q20553.en: The sign shown warns that traffic cannot flow in both directions at the same time.

explain.short: In the narrow passage the two directions must take turns, so they cannot move at the same time.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'contemporaneamente' means at the same time: that is exactly what is not possible here.

sceneParams.caption: Both directions can't pass at the same time

q20554.en: The sign shown warns that traffic is allowed in one direction on even days and in the other on odd days.

explain.short: The sign is about taking turns at a narrow passage, not about even and odd days.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'giorni pari' and 'giorni dispari' (even and odd days) belong to parking rules, not to this sign.

sceneParams.caption: Not even/odd days: give way to oncoming cars

q20555.en: The sign shown warns of right of way in alternating one-way traffic.

explain.short: This sign takes priority away from you: you must give way. The sign that gives you priority is a blue square with a white arrow.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'diritto di precedenza' (right of way) is the opposite: here you GIVE way.

sceneParams.caption: You give way here, you do not have priority

q20556.en: The sign shown, on a one-way carriageway, warns of the start of two-way traffic.

explain.short: This sign is about a narrow passage on a two-way road; the start of two-way traffic has a different, triangular warning sign.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'inizio del doppio senso' (start of two-way traffic) is a danger sign, not this round priority sign.

sceneParams.caption: Not start of two-way traffic: give way at narrowing

q20557.en: The sign shown warns of the end of one-way traffic.

explain.short: It does not end a one-way road; it tells you to give way to oncoming vehicles at a narrow passage.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'fine del senso unico' (end of one-way) is a different sign.

sceneParams.caption: Not end of one-way: give way to oncoming cars

q20558.en: The sign shown warns of the end of the right of way in alternating one-way traffic.

explain.short: Nothing ends here: the sign starts an obligation to give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of right of way) is the wrong idea; you never had priority here.

sceneParams.caption: Nothing ends: you must give way

q20559.en: The sign shown is found on one-way roads.

explain.short: On a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic; this sign is used on two-way roads with a narrow passage.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'strade a senso unico' (one-way roads) is the trap: the black arrow shows traffic coming the other way.

sceneParams.caption: Used on two-way roads, not one-way roads

q20560.en: The sign shown is a mandatory (prescription) sign.

explain.short: Priority signs belong to the family of 'segnali di prescrizione' (rule signs), like prohibition and obligation signs.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'prescrizione' (prescription) is the big family: it includes priority signs.

sceneParams.caption: Priority signs are prescription signs

q20561.en: The sign shown can be placed on a road where part of the carriageway is closed off.

explain.short: If part of the road is closed (for example by works), the free part becomes a narrow passage, so one side must give way.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'sbarrata' means closed off: that creates the narrow passage.

sceneParams.caption: Half road closed: one side gives way

q20562.en: The sign shown can be placed on a road with a narrow passage.

explain.short: A narrow passage is the typical place for this sign.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'strettoia' means narrow passage.

sceneParams.caption: Typical place: a narrow passage

q20563.en: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

explain.short: The black arrow shows oncoming vehicles: they pass first, you wait.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'senso opposto' means the opposite direction.

sceneParams.caption: Oncoming vehicles go first

q20564.en: The sign shown orders you to give way in alternating one-way traffic.

explain.short: This is the sign's name: in the narrow passage traffic goes one direction at a time, and you give way.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'prescrive' means orders: it is a rule, not advice.

sceneParams.caption: One direction at a time: you give way

q20565.en: The sign shown is found before a narrow passage that, as a rule, lets only one line of vehicles through.

explain.short: Normally the narrow passage is so tight that only one line of vehicles fits, so the two directions take turns.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'di norma' means as a rule: usually, not in every single case.

sceneParams.caption: As a rule only one line fits

q20566.en: The sign shown is found before any narrowing of the carriageway.

explain.short: Not every narrowing needs it: only one where two vehicles cannot pass each other.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'qualsiasi' (any) is the trap word: the sign is not used for every narrowing.

sceneParams.caption: Not any narrowing: only one-line passages

q20567.en: The sign shown is a prohibition sign.

explain.short: It looks like a round red-ringed sign, but it belongs to the priority signs, not to the prohibition signs.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'divieto' (prohibition) is the trap: the red ring makes you think of a ban.

sceneParams.caption: A priority sign, not a prohibition sign

q20568.en: The sign shown is placed at the start of a one-way road.

explain.short: There are oncoming vehicles, so the road is two-way; the sign is placed before a narrow passage.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) is the trap: the black arrow shows traffic coming the other way.

sceneParams.caption: Not one-way start: narrow passage on two-way road

q20569.en: The sign shown obliges you, at junctions, to give way to vehicles coming from both the right and the left.

explain.short: The sign is about oncoming vehicles at a narrow passage, not about junctions. Giving way to both sides at a junction is the triangle 'dare precedenza'.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'negli incroci' (at junctions) is the trap: this sign is for narrow passages.

sceneParams.caption: Not junctions: oncoming cars at a narrow passage

keywords.it: sia da destra che da sinistra

q20570.en: The sign shown is a danger sign.

explain.short: Danger signs are triangles. This round sign is a priority sign.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'pericolo' (danger) is wrong: danger signs are red triangles.

sceneParams.caption: Round priority sign, not a danger triangle

q20571.en: The sign shown warns of right of way in alternating one-way traffic.

explain.short: Here you give way. Right of way at a narrow passage is a blue square sign with a white arrow.
explain.rule: The round sign with a red arrow (your direction) and a black arrow (the other direction) is 'dare precedenza nel senso unico alternato' (give way in alternating one-way traffic). It stands before a 'strettoia' (narrow passage) where only one line of vehicles fits: you must let oncoming vehicles pass first.
explain.trap: 'diritto di precedenza' (right of way) is the opposite of what this sign says.

sceneParams.caption: You give way here, you do not have priority

q20572.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is green.

explain.short: A working traffic light is stronger than the sign: on green you may go.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'luce verde' (green light): the light, not the sign, decides.

sceneParams.caption: Green light beats the sign: you go

q20573.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way if the light is off.

explain.short: When the light is off, it gives no orders, so the sign applies: give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'spento' (off): a dead light means the sign is in charge.

sceneParams.caption: Light off: the sign applies, give way

q20574.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is red but the traffic officer orders us to go.

explain.short: A traffic officer's order is stronger than both the light and the sign: if he says go, you go.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'agente del traffico' (traffic officer): his orders beat the red light.

sceneParams.caption: Officer says go: obey the officer

q20575.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way if the light is flashing yellow.

explain.short: Flashing yellow only means 'be careful'; it gives no right to go, so the sign applies.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'lampeggiante gialla' (flashing yellow) is not a green light: the sign decides.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing yellow: the sign applies, give way

q20576.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way even if the light is green.

explain.short: On green the traffic light is in charge and you may go; the sign counts only when the light is off or flashing yellow.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'anche se' (even if) is the trap: green beats the sign.

sceneParams.caption: Green light beats the sign: you go

q20577.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is flashing yellow.

explain.short: Flashing yellow gives no priority: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'gialla lampeggiante' (flashing yellow) is not green.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing yellow: no priority, give way

q20578.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we have priority if the light is green but the traffic officer orders us to stop.

explain.short: The officer's order beats the green light: if he says stop, you stop.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'ci ordina di fermarci' (orders us to stop): the officer wins over green.

sceneParams.caption: Officer says stop: you stop, even on green

q20579.en: With the sign shown and a three-light traffic light, we must give way if the light is off and the traffic officer orders us to go.

explain.short: The officer's order beats the sign: if he says go, you go.
explain.rule: A working traffic light is stronger than this sign, and a traffic officer is stronger than both. Green light, or the officer says go: you go first. Light off or flashing yellow: the sign applies and you give way to oncoming vehicles.
explain.trap: 'ci ordina di passare' (orders us to go): the officer wins over the sign.

sceneParams.caption: Officer says go: obey the officer

q20580.en: The sign shown calls for more caution because you no longer have right of way.

explain.short: Your road loses its priority, so at the next junctions you must watch other traffic more carefully.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'non si ha più' means you no longer have it.

sceneParams.caption: Priority road ends: be more careful

q20581.en: With the sign shown, the driver, unless another sign says otherwise, must give way to vehicles coming from the right.

explain.short: After the end of the priority road the general rule returns: give way to the right.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'salvo diverso ulteriore segnale' means unless another sign says something different.

sceneParams.caption: General rule again: give way to the right

q20582.en: The sign shown is a priority sign.

explain.short: It belongs to the priority signs, like 'dare precedenza', STOP and 'diritto di precedenza'.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'segnale di precedenza' (priority sign) is the right family.

sceneParams.caption: End of priority road: a priority sign

q20583.en: The sign shown indicates that the road no longer has right of way.

explain.short: The black bar crosses out the priority sign: the priority road is over.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'non gode più' means no longer has.

sceneParams.caption: This road no longer has priority

q20584.en: The sign shown can be followed by the STOP sign (stop and give way).

explain.short: After the priority road ends, the next junction can have a STOP or a give-way sign.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'può essere seguito' means can come after it: possible, not always.

sceneParams.caption: Next junction may have a STOP

q20585.en: The sign shown changes the previous priority rules at junctions.

explain.short: Before, you had priority at junctions; now the general rule returns, so the rules change.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'modifica' means changes: your priority at junctions is no longer the same.

sceneParams.caption: Junction rules change: priority ends

q20586.en: The sign shown is an information sign.

explain.short: It is a priority sign, not an information sign.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'indicazione' (information) is the wrong family.

sceneParams.caption: A priority sign, not an information sign

q20587.en: The sign shown warns that you are driving on a road with right of way.

explain.short: The black bar means the opposite: the right of way has ended.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: The missing word is 'fine' (end): the bar crosses out the priority.

sceneParams.caption: Not a priority road: priority has ended

q20588.en: The sign shown obliges you to stop at the junction.

explain.short: Only the STOP sign obliges you to stop. This sign only says your priority has ended.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'arrestarsi' (to stop) is the trap: no stop is required by this sign.

sceneParams.caption: No stop required: priority just ends

q20589.en: The sign shown shows the layout of the main road.

explain.short: The layout of the main road is shown by a panel with a thick line; this sign only marks the end of priority.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'andamento della strada principale' (layout of the main road) is a different panel.

sceneParams.caption: No road layout: only end of priority

q20590.en: The sign shown always warns of a junction with priority to the right.

explain.short: It does not always announce a junction; and the next junction may have other signs, like STOP.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap word.

sceneParams.caption: Not always a junction: priority just ends

q20591.en: The sign shown warns of the end of the obligation imposed before.

explain.short: A priority road was a right, not an obligation; the sign ends a right, not a ban or duty.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'obbligo' (obligation) is the trap: what ends is a right ('diritto').

sceneParams.caption: A right ends, not an obligation

q20592.en: The sign shown warns of a dead-end road.

explain.short: A dead end is a blue square information sign with a red-topped white T. This sign is the end of priority.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'strada senza uscita' (dead end) is a different sign.

sceneParams.caption: Not a dead end: end of priority road

q20593.en: The sign shown indicates that the general priority rule is back in force.

explain.short: When the priority road ends, the general rule (give way to the right) applies again.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'ripristino' means return: the normal rule comes back.

sceneParams.caption: General rule is back: right has priority

q20594.en: The sign shown indicates that a road with right of way ends.

explain.short: That is its name: 'fine del diritto di precedenza'.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'termina' means ends.

sceneParams.caption: The priority road ends here

q20595.en: The sign shown indicates that after it you will, as a rule, have to give way to the right.

explain.short: Once priority ends, the general rule applies: vehicles from the right go first.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'di norma' means as a rule: unless other signs say otherwise.

sceneParams.caption: After it: as a rule, give way to the right

q20596.en: The sign shown indicates the end of right of way on urban roads too.

explain.short: The sign works the same inside and outside towns.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'anche sulle strade urbane' means on town roads too.

sceneParams.caption: Valid on town roads too

q20597.en: The sign shown indicates the end of a motorway.

explain.short: The end of a motorway is a green sign with a crossed-out motorway symbol. This one ends priority.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'autostrada' (motorway) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not end of motorway: end of priority

q20598.en: The sign shown indicates the end of a one-way road.

explain.short: It has nothing to do with one-way roads: it ends priority.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not end of one-way: end of priority

q20599.en: The sign shown indicates the end of a two-way road.

explain.short: It has nothing to do with the number of directions: it ends priority.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'doppio senso' (two-way) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not end of two-way: end of priority

q20600.en: The sign shown indicates the end of the speed limit.

explain.short: The end of a speed limit is a round white sign with the crossed-out number. This one ends priority.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'limite di velocità' (speed limit) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not end of speed limit: end of priority

q20601.en: The sign shown indicates the end of all prohibitions.

explain.short: The end of all prohibitions is a round white sign with grey diagonal lines. This one ends priority.
explain.rule: The white-and-yellow diamond crossed by a black bar is 'fine del diritto di precedenza' (end of the priority road), a priority sign. Your road loses its priority: the general rule comes back, so at junctions you normally give way to vehicles from the right, unless other signs say otherwise.
explain.trap: 'tutti i divieti' (all prohibitions) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not end of all bans: end of priority

q20602.en: The sign shown warns of a junction with less important roads.

explain.short: The thick line is your main road; the thin line is the minor road that crosses it.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'minore importanza' means less important: the side roads are minor.

sceneParams.caption: Junction with minor roads: you go first

q20603.en: The sign shown warns of a junction where you have priority over vehicles coming from the side roads.

explain.short: Vehicles from the minor roads must give way to you.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'strade secondarie' means side roads (minor roads).

sceneParams.caption: Side-road vehicles wait for you

q20604.en: The sign shown warns of a junction with a road that has no right of way.

explain.short: The crossing road is minor: it has no priority over yours.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'senza diritto di precedenza' means without right of way: the other road, not yours.

sceneParams.caption: The crossing road has no priority

q20605.en: The sign shown, at the junction, gives us priority over vehicles coming from both the right and the left.

explain.short: The thin line crosses on both sides, so vehicles from both sides must wait for you.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'sia da destra che da sinistra' (both right and left): the minor road is on both sides.

sceneParams.caption: Priority over both right and left

keywords.it: sia da destra che da sinistra

q20606.en: The sign shown loses its effect when a traffic officer is directing traffic.

explain.short: A traffic officer's orders are stronger than any sign.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'perde la sua efficacia' means stops counting: the officer is in charge.

sceneParams.caption: An officer's orders beat the sign

q20607.en: The sign shown can be preceded by the priority road sign.

explain.short: On a priority road (yellow diamond), this triangle can warn of a junction along it.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'può essere preceduto' means can come after: the diamond can appear earlier.

sceneParams.caption: May come along a priority road

q20608.en: The sign shown warns that you must slow down to make sure you are given priority.

explain.short: You have priority, but you must slow down and check the others really stop.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'accertare' means make sure: priority is not a reason to rush.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down and check they give way

q20609.en: The sign shown warns of a junction where you have priority.

explain.short: The thick vertical line is your road: you have priority at the junction.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'si ha la precedenza' means you have priority.

sceneParams.caption: Junction where you have priority

q20610.en: The sign shown warns of a merge from both the right and the left.

explain.short: It is a crossroads, not a merge: the minor road crosses yours.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'confluenza' (merge) is the trap: here the road crosses, it does not join.

sceneParams.caption: A crossroads with minor roads, not a merge

keywords.it: sia da destra che da sinistra

q20611.en: The sign shown forbids turning left at the junction.

explain.short: It does not forbid anything: it tells you that you have priority at the junction.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'vieta' (forbids) is the trap: this is a priority sign, not a ban.

sceneParams.caption: No ban: you have priority at the junction

q20612.en: The sign shown warns of a junction where you have priority over vehicles from the left, while you must give way to those from the right.

explain.short: You have priority over BOTH sides; you do not give way to the right.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'si deve dare la precedenza a quelli provenienti da destra' is wrong: the right must wait too.

sceneParams.caption: Priority over both sides, the right too

q20613.en: The sign shown is placed on motorways.

explain.short: Motorways have no level junctions, so this junction sign is not used there.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'autostrade' (motorways) is the trap: there are no crossroads on motorways.

sceneParams.caption: No crossroads on motorways

q20614.en: The sign shown is placed no more than 25 metres from the junction.

explain.short: Like danger signs, it is placed well before the junction, about 150 m outside towns, not within 25 m.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'non più di 25 metri' (no more than 25 metres) is too close.

sceneParams.caption: Placed ahead (150 m outside towns), not at 25 m

q20615.en: The sign shown warns of a junction where you must give way.

explain.short: Here YOU have priority; the others give way to you.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'bisogna dare la precedenza' (you must give way) is the opposite.

sceneParams.caption: You have priority, you do not give way

q20616.en: The sign shown warns of acceleration lanes on the right and on the left.

explain.short: The thin line is a minor road crossing, not an acceleration lane.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line crossed by a thin line is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' (junction with priority). A crossroads with minor roads is coming: you go first over vehicles from the right AND from the left, but slow down and check they give way.
explain.trap: 'corsie di accelerazione' (acceleration lanes) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Minor roads crossing, not acceleration lanes

q20617.en: The sign shown warns that a less important road crosses on the right.

explain.short: The thin line joins from the right: it is a minor road.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'minore importanza' means less important.

sceneParams.caption: Minor road on the right: you go first

q20618.en: The sign shown warns of a junction with a side road joining from the right.

explain.short: The thin line shows a minor road coming in from the right.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'si immette da destra' means joins from the right.

sceneParams.caption: Side road joins from the right

q20619.en: With the sign shown you must be careful because you are approaching a junction.

explain.short: A junction is coming: even with priority, you must drive carefully.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'prudenza' means caution.

sceneParams.caption: Junction ahead: drive carefully

q20620.en: The sign shown is a priority sign.

explain.short: Though it is a triangle, it belongs to the priority signs because it tells you who goes first.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'segnale di precedenza' (priority sign): the triangle shape can mislead you.

sceneParams.caption: A priority sign, even if it is a triangle

q20621.en: The sign shown warns of the junction with a road without right of way.

explain.short: The road on the right is minor: it has no priority over yours.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'senza diritto di precedenza' refers to the other road, not yours.

sceneParams.caption: The side road has no priority

q20622.en: The sign shown warns of a junction where the driver has priority over vehicles coming from the right.

explain.short: Vehicles from the side road on the right must give way to you.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'da destra' (from the right): normally the right goes first, but here YOU do.

sceneParams.caption: You go first, the right waits

q20623.en: The sign shown warns of a dead-end road on the right.

explain.short: The thin line is a side road, not a dead end. A dead end is a blue square sign.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'strada senza uscita' (dead end) is a different sign.

sceneParams.caption: Side road on the right, not a dead end

q20624.en: The sign shown forbids turning right.

explain.short: It forbids nothing: it tells you that you have priority over the side road.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'vieta' (forbids) is the trap: it is not a prohibition sign.

sceneParams.caption: No ban: you have priority

q20625.en: The sign shown is placed on motorway acceleration lanes.

explain.short: It is used on ordinary roads before a junction, not on motorway lanes.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'corsie di accelerazione delle autostrade' (motorway acceleration lanes) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Ordinary road junction, not a motorway lane

q20626.en: The sign shown warns of a road entry with an acceleration lane.

explain.short: The thin line is a minor road at a junction, not an acceleration lane.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'corsia di accelerazione' (acceleration lane) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Minor road junction, not an acceleration lane

q20627.en: The sign shown warns of a junction where the driver must stop and give way to vehicles coming from the right.

explain.short: The opposite is true: you have priority over the side road on the right, and no stop is required.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'obbligo di fermarsi' (must stop) is the trap: that is the STOP sign.

sceneParams.caption: No stop: you have priority over the right

q20628.en: The sign shown indicates a lay-by on the right.

explain.short: A lay-by is a blue information sign. This red triangle warns of a minor road on the right.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a thick vertical line and a thin line joining from the right is 'intersezione con diritto di precedenza' with a side road on the right. A minor road joins from the right: you have priority over vehicles coming out of it, but be careful.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' (lay-by) is a different sign.

sceneParams.caption: Side road on the right, not a lay-by
